rationale: Activating follows the casting steps (602.2b/602.2), the 'Activate only if you control three or more artifacts' restriction is checked when the activation is announced (601.2e/602.5), and mana abilities aren't activated until 601.2g, after that check.

602.2a puts the ability on the stack as its own object controlled by the activating player, 602.2b makes the rest of activation follow 601.2b-i, and 601.2g places the mana-ability window after the ability is already on the stack, so losing control of Jade Mage afterward changes nothing.

Same activation chain as the Jade Mage case (602.2a controller, 602.2b process, 601.2g mana-ability timing), plus 107.5 for {T} meaning 'tap this permanent' regardless of controller, and 601.2e/602.5a for legality including summoning sickness being checked before mana abilities are activated.

Venarian Gold is put onto the battlefield without ever being cast, so X is 0: 107.3g treats {X} in a mana cost as 0 outside the stack and 107.3m states the value of X for the permanent, and hence its enters-the-battlefield ability, is 0.

303.4f requires the player putting an Aura onto the battlefield to choose a legal object per its enchant ability as it enters, which a card entering simultaneously isn't; 303.4g covers the case where no legal object exists.
113.6 states that abilities of objects other than instants and sorceries function only while on the battlefield, so Nicol Bolas's activated ability can't be activated from the graveyard.

The 'enters tapped' text is a static ability generating a replacement effect (603.6d), and 614.12 checks the permanent's characteristics taking already-existing continuous effects into account, so Alpine Moon has stripped it; 603.10/603.6a check trigger conditions against the objects and continuous effects existing immediately after the permanent enters.

301.5c states an Equipment that's also a creature can't equip a creature and can't equip itself; 701.3b/301.5b state the Equipment simply doesn't move when an effect tries to attach it illegally, so the ability resolves and does nothing.

614.12 requires checking the permanent as it would exist on the battlefield taking into account continuous effects that already exist, so under Humility the Clever Impersonator has no copy ability to apply as it enters.

Same shape as the Alpine Moon case: 603.6d/614.12 make the 'enters tapped' replacement effect check the Temple as it would exist with Blood Sun applied, and 603.10/603.6a check the ETB trigger condition against the objects and effects existing right after it enters.

Alpine Moon's ability removal and mana-ability grant apply in layer 6 (613.1f), its land-subtype removal and Skilled Animator's type change apply in layer 4 (613.1d), and the 5/5 base power and toughness is set in sublayer 7b (613.4b), so the two effects coexist rather than overwrite each other.
608.2b says a spell with some but not all targets illegal still resolves; 701.14b says that if either creature instructed to fight is an illegal target or gone, neither fights or deals damage.

702.19b requires the trample attacker's controller to assign lethal damage to blockers before any damage goes to the player, and its example explicitly covers a blocker with protection; 702.16e is why that assigned damage is then prevented.
Witch Hunt says players can't gain life, and 614.17b states that if an event can't happen a player can't choose to pay a cost that includes that event, so Invigorate's alternative cost is unpayable.
Sulfuric Vortex replaces the life gain rather than making it impossible, and 118.11 states that a cost whose actions are modified by effects has still been paid.

702.15c states last known information determines whether the source had lifelink when it's no longer in the zone it was expected to be in; 608.2h is the general LKI rule for information about the ability's own source.

113.7a states the triggered ability exists on the stack independently of the Curse Artifact, so destroying the Aura doesn't stop the trigger; 118.1 defines a cost as an action necessary to stop another action from taking place, so failing to sacrifice means the 2 damage happens.

510.1/510.1c make damage assignment a turn-based action in the combat damage step, with a blocked creature's damage divided among its blockers as its controller chooses; 702.2b destroys any creature dealt damage by a deathtouch source as a state-based action.

Both type-changing effects apply in layer 4 (613.1d) in timestamp order (613.7/613.3), so Starfield's later effect makes Iroas a creature; the base power/toughness setting applies in sublayer 7b (613.4b).

608.2c carries out Madcap Experiment's instructions in written order, so Platinum Emperion is already on the battlefield when the damage happens; 614.17 covers effects stating something can't happen, so the life total doesn't change.

120.3 states damage may have one or more results and 120.3f/702.15b make the lifelink life gain an additional, independent result; 120.3a is the life-loss result that Platinum Emperion makes impossible.
608.2b states a spell is countered on resolution if all of its targets are illegal, so Release the Gremlins does nothing at all.
608.2c has the resolving spell's instructions carried out in the order written, so the Walker is already destroyed when the artifact check happens.
608.2c puts the token creation before the free cast, so the Servos exist to be sacrificed; 118.9d/601.2f state that additional costs still apply on top of an alternative cost.

603.10 states that the objects existing immediately after the event, and the continuous effects existing then, determine whether a trigger condition was met, and in the graveyard Yixlid Jailer has stripped Dread's abilities.

704.3 checks state-based actions only when a player would receive priority, never mid-resolution; 704.5g is the lethal-damage destruction; 608.2n puts Starfall into the graveyard as the final part of its resolution, which is what grows Tarmogoyf to 3/4.

Melira's ability removal and Inkmoth Nexus's infect grant are both layer 6 effects applied in timestamp order (613.7/613.3), so the later grant wins; 702.90b/120.3b state infect damage to a player gives poison counters instead of causing life loss, which Melira makes impossible.

609.7a states that choosing a permanent spell as the damage source makes the effect apply to damage dealt by the permanent that spell becomes; 400.7c states the same for prevention effects across that zone change.
702.19b governs assigning lethal damage to the blocker before trampling over, 702.4b creates the two combat damage steps, and 704.5g kills the blocker between them when enough damage was assigned.
702.16d states a permanent with protection can't be equipped by Equipment of that quality and that such Equipment becomes unattached as a state-based action; 704.5n is that state-based action.

Color-changing is layer 5 and ability removal layer 6 (613.1e/613.1), so Painter's Servant's color effect still applies despite Gift of Tusks; within layer 6 the Sword's protection grant has the later timestamp (613.7, and 613.7e for the new timestamp on attaching); 702.16d/704.5n then unattach it.

608.2c carries out Kolaghan's Command's modes in written order, 701.19a has the regeneration shield consumed by the first destruction, and 704.5g then destroys the Wicker Witch for lethal damage with no shield left.
Twinstrike's hellbent clause replaces its own effect, and 614.15/616.1a state that self-replacement effects are applied before other replacement effects such as Swans of Bryn Argoll's.

702.89a is the umbra armor replacement that redirects the destruction to Drake Umbra; 616.1 governs choosing among replacement effects modifying the same event, leaving only one destruction and therefore 2 life.
702.89a replaces the creature's destruction with destroying the Aura, so no creature was destroyed and Overwhelming Forces draws nothing.
702.89a makes Felidar Umbra the card destroyed instead of Torsten; 303.4f makes Allen choose a legal creature for it to enchant as it returns to the battlefield under his control.
702.40a defines storm as copying the spell for each spell cast before it that turn, so a spell cast in response isn't counted.

608.2h fixes the 'if it doesn't have that ability' check at the moment Musician's ability resolves, when Snakeform has stripped the Craw Wurm's abilities; 611.2a gives the granted ability no duration, so it persists after Snakeform expires and the printed instance returns.

113.11, applied in layer 6 per 613.1f, stops Crowd's Favor from granting first strike; 613.1g applies power/toughness changes in layer 7 afterward, where the Bears count as having no abilities for Muraganda Petroglyphs.

Dream Leash's restriction is worded to apply only as targets are chosen while casting (601.2c); on resolution 608.2b rechecks only legality under 'enchant permanent', which the now-untapped permanent still satisfies.

602.2a/113.7a make the activated ability on the stack its own object, distinct from the identically worded printed ability it references as 'this ability'; Cytoshape's copy effect (707.2, applied in layer 1 per 613.1a) is what gives the Licid that printed ability afresh.

510.2 deals all combat damage simultaneously, 704.3 performs state-based actions (both creatures dying) before anyone gets priority, 510.3a/603.3 then put the trigger on the stack, and 400.7 means the Thoctar that left the battlefield can't be found to receive a counter.

511.2 has the 'at end of combat' delayed trigger trigger only as the end of combat step begins; 510.3/511.1 give players priority during the combat damage step and again in the end of combat step before that trigger resolves.
608.2c has the resolving spell's instructions followed in the order written, and the discard instruction is separate from the counter-unless clause, so it happens regardless.

702.4b creates the two combat damage steps, 702.15b/120.3f gain the life from the first-strike damage, and 611.3a means Gavony Ironwright's fateful hour static ability stops applying the moment the life total rises above 5.

614.12 determines applicable replacement effects from the permanent as it would exist, so Gather Specimens doesn't apply until Copy Artifact's copy choice makes it a creature; 616.1f/616.1 then repeat the process with the newly applicable control-changing effect.

616.1 governs applying two replacement effects to the same event and 616.1b requires the control-changing effect (Gather Specimens) to be chosen first, so Nico is the entering permanent's controller when the copy choice is made.

613.8a makes Life and Limb's effect dependent on Blood Moon's, since applying Blood Moon changes what Life and Limb applies to, 613.8b makes it wait until afterward, and 305.7 states that becoming a Mountain strips the old land types so Murmuring Bosk is no longer a Forest.

613.8a/613.8b make Blood Moon's effect dependent on Life and Limb's and hold it until afterward; 305.7 states the resulting Mountain loses its old land types and abilities and gains the {R} mana ability.

613.8a establishes the mutual dependency, 613.8b says a dependency loop is ignored, 613.7 then applies the earlier-timestamped Life and Limb first, and 305.7 gives the Mountain result for both permanents.
